summary: Eleven comment-endorsed tools, datasets, apps, articles, videos, and books from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 11 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: skills-sdlc
items.source_story_title: Ask HN: How do you manage skills files?
items.summary: A version-controlled collection of software-development skills with a symlink installer.
items.why_included: Its user described a practical, continuously tested workflow for sharing skills across machines.
items.evidence: The commenter keeps these skills in Git and updates installations by advancing the repository.

evidence_sources.author: gregwebs
evidence_sources.excerpt: I have a git repo with my skills for software development [1]. There is an installer script that symlinks to the skills. Updating the skills on a machine is then just a matter of advancing the git repo.

items.name: SX
items.source_story_title: Ask HN: How do you manage skills files?
items.summary: A Git-backed tool for managing and sharing AI coding-agent skills.
items.why_included: A current user finds it useful despite quirks and uses it for skills management.
items.evidence: The commenter gave SX a positive first-hand assessment after using it to manage skills.

evidence_sources.author: nhod
evidence_sources.excerpt: It has its quirks, but overall I find it to be very useful.

items.name: Radiance vLLM MXFP4
items.source_story_title: Speculative Decoding in vLLM on AMD GPUs
items.summary: A vLLM fork adding MXFP4 and early PARO quantization for AMD R9700 GPUs.
items.why_included: An AMD GPU user called the fork excellent and uses it daily.
items.evidence: The commenter endorsed the MXFP4 fork as their current daily driver.

evidence_sources.author: intothemild
evidence_sources.excerpt: The MXFP4 fork is excellent too. Its my daily driver right now.

items.name: Ctx
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Engrim – A universal, local-first SQLite memory engine for AI CLIs
items.summary: A memory plugin that lets coding agents recover context from earlier sessions.
items.why_included: A months-long user said it largely eliminated their need for session compaction.
items.evidence: The commenter reported using the plugin for months and now usually starts fresh sessions instead of compacting.

evidence_sources.author: flippant
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using another memory plugin [1] for the past couple months. Since this change, I almost never run session compaction.
